name: Audrey Kahn
life: “I still remember hiring a chair by the hour during a wet summer.” On Saturday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Audrey pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I rented the parasol by the hour. Its whole day's income is now sitting over a street chess game.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. Audrey has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Audrey turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
personality: Audrey loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To recover the day's rental or agree to forgive it.
family: Jorge Dias is Audrey’s first cousin once removed. Audrey brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Jorge makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Overdue by a lifetime*, Jorge says, “I borrowed it after failing a reading test.”
connections: Aubrey Yates (hotel manager). They trace a striped hotel parasol from the hire stand to the chess game.

reactions.situation: A hotel worker asks to throw the patched umbrella away
reactions.response: Audrey puts the patched umbrella aside until the owner can explain the repair.
reactions.asWritten: A hotel worker asks to throw the patched umbrella away. Audrey puts the patched umbrella aside until the owner can explain the repair.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Audrey keeps the documents out of view and lets the person claiming it identify it before hearing any details.

reactions.situation: If a stranger asks to hear a private story
reactions.response: Audrey offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
